findings.reason: naming `reckon/ledger.py` as the index owner lets the plan extend the one index built from the files and drop `run_store.db` entirely, instead of maintaining two rebuildable indexes over the same rows.
findings.text: the plan's §7 declares per-run files the record and "the SQLite store … an index built from them", but `reckon/ledger.py` already maintains a rebuildable SQLite index over those same per-run files (`_run_index_path` at reckon/ledger.py:785, `index_stamp` at :793, `_indexed_data` at :864), keyed on the picker projection; `reckon/run_store.py` adds a second database (`run_store.db`, keys `member/node/project/completed_at/backend`) over one corpus — two indexes, two shapes, two migration paths, exactly the split that made the old single file cost a full read

findings.reason: the plan should extend the roster owner at `reckon/ledger.py` rather than carry a parallel table, since the two will drift the first time a member is written on one side only.
findings.text: §2 proposes that members and holds "become their own tables", implemented as the `members`/`holds` tables in `reckon/run_store.py` (`append_member` at run_store.py:514), but the roster is owned by `reckon/ledger.py` (`members` at ledger.py:1469, `register_member` at ledger.py:1746; the companion plan moved it to `crew/members.json`), which every dispatch already reads; a second roster table is a fork with no reader wired to it

findings.reason: the plan should delete the export stage and state that the per-run file IS the export, removing a second writer of the same record that would otherwise need to be kept in step with the promotion path.
findings.text: §4 keeps a separate "export" mechanism — a committed file "written whenever it changes", "reconstructible from the database at any time" — but §7 makes the per-run file the record written at promotion by `ledger.append_run` (reckon/ledger.py); the export stage is a thin layer over that existing write and its stated reconstructive direction (file rebuilt from the database) is the reverse of §7's (index rebuilt from the files); the plan never says why `ledger.append_run`/`ledger.write` cannot carry the record

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/run_store.py` hides schema creation, in-place migration, cache refresh and the durable/detail split behind a small interface (`append`, `sync_run`, `get_run`, `get_detail`, `compare`, `import_ledger`); it is deeper than the file scan it replaces.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's §7 store is a second SQLite index over the per-run files, duplicating the rebuildable index that `reckon/ledger.py` now owns.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §7 reuses the existing writer and reader (`ledger.append_run`, `ledger.load`), the crew.json `runs` list and the companion plan rather than proposing a new serialiser, and §1 measured the existing ledger's shape rather than assuming it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan its §4 "export" stage retained beside §7's per-run write, a thin layer over `ledger.append_run` whose direction §7 already reversed.
